newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Uruguay ex-prisoner to head rights rights group.
newsitem.headline: Uruguay ex-prisoner to head rights rights group.

text.p: Uruguay's vice-president Hugo Batalla, a political prisoner during military rule in his country, was on Monday elected chairman of a key body which works to protect the human rights of parliamentarians.

The Geneva-based Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) said Batalla, who is also president of the Uruguay Senate, won the post at a special session of the group, the Committee on the Human Rights of Parliamentarians.

The Committee is the IPU's specialised body looking into violations of the rights of members of legislatures around the world -- mainly measures taken against them for exercising the right to free speech.
Batalla, a member of the Uruguayan parliament since 1962, was a member of the country's Chamber of Deputies until a military coup in 1973.
Twice jailed for campaigning against the military regime, he was elected to the Senate when civilian rule was restored in 1985.

He took over running of the Committee, which meets four times a year and usually applies backstage pressure to achieve settlement of cases it takes up, from Nicos Anastasiades, a member of the Cyprus House of Representatives.
Australian parliamentarian Clyde Holding was elected vice-president of the Committee.
